3. Identify and remove samples with outlier porosity values. Show how the outliers were determined and report the number of samples removed.¶

Outlier Removal via Z-Score Filtering

Given a dataset with a variable $X$ (Porosity (%)), outlier removal is performed as follows:

  • Calculate the mean $ \mu $ and standard deviation $ \sigma $ of $X$.
  • For each observation $x_i$, compute its z-score: $ z_i = \dfrac{x_i - \mu}{\sigma} $.
  • Determine the absolute value of each z-score, $ |z_i| $.
  • Define an outlier threshold (e.g., $2$). An observation is considered an outlier if $ |z_i| \geq 2 $.
  • Remove any observations where $ |z_i| \geq 2 $; retain those with $ |z_i| < 2 $.

Threshold = 1

  • Number of rows removed: 65
  • Percentage of dataset removed: 34.03%

Threshold = 2

  • Number of rows removed: 4
  • Percentage of dataset removed: 2.09%

Threshold = 3

  • Number of rows removed: 0
  • Percentage of dataset removed: 0.00%

I used a threshold of 2 for this dataset.

from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline

# apply pca
def apply_pca(df:pd.DataFrame, n_components:int)->pd.DataFrame:

    scaler = StandardScaler()
    pca = PCA(n_components=n_components)
    pipeline = make_pipeline(scaler, pca)
    pipeline.fit(df)
    pca_features = pipeline.transform(df)
    pca_features_df = pd.DataFrame(pca_features)
    pca_features_df.columns = [f"PCA_{i}" for i in range(n_components)]
    print(f"PCA features shape: {pca_features_df.shape}")
    return pca_features_df

pca_features = apply_pca(df, 2)
pca_features.plot(kind='scatter', x=['PCA_0'], y=['PCA_1'])

# z score outlier removal
def remove_outliers(df: pd.DataFrame, column_name: str, threshold: int = 3) -> pd.DataFrame:
    old_len = len(df)
    series = df[column_name]
    z_scores = (series - series.mean()) / series.std()
    abs_z_scores = np.abs(z_scores)
    filtered_entries = (abs_z_scores < threshold)
    df_filtered = df[filtered_entries]
    new_len = len(df_filtered)
    percent_removed = (old_len - new_len) / old_len * 100  # percent removed
    print(f"Number of rows removed: {old_len - new_len}")
    print(f"Percentage of dataset removed: {percent_removed:.2f}%")
    return df_filtered

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import math

# 1. Crossplot with reg. lines.
def plot_cross(df: pd.DataFrame):
    num_cols = len(df.columns)
    r2_matrix = np.empty((num_cols, num_cols))
    r2_matrix[:] = np.nan  # fill cells that are not computed

    fig, axs = plt.subplots(num_cols, num_cols, figsize=(15,15))
    for i in range(num_cols):
        for j in range(num_cols):
            ax = axs[i][j]
            if i == j:
                # Remove diagonal plots (or leave blank)
                ax.set_visible(False)
            else:
                # Create scatter plot for non-diagonals
                ax.scatter(df[df.columns[i]], df[df.columns[j]], s=10)
                
                # Fit linear regression: slope & intercept
                x = df[df.columns[i]]
                y = df[df.columns[j]]
                slope, intercept = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
                
                # Plot regression line over the current x-range
                x_vals = np.array(ax.get_xlim())
                y_vals = intercept + slope * x_vals
                ax.plot(x_vals, y_vals, '--', color='red')
                
                # Calculate predicted values and R²
                y_pred = intercept + slope * x
                ss_res = np.sum((y - y_pred)**2)
                ss_tot = np.sum((y - y.mean())**2)
                r2 = 1 - (ss_res/ss_tot) if ss_tot != 0 else np.nan
                r2_matrix[i, j] = r2
                
                # Label axes for clarity (optional)
                if j == 0:
                    ax.set_ylabel(df.columns[i], fontsize=8)
                if i == num_cols - 1:
                    ax.set_xlabel(df.columns[j], fontsize=8)
                    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    return r2_matrix

# 2. r2 plot
def plot_r2_heatmap(r2_matrix: np.ndarray, columns: pd.Index):
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 10))
    sns.set(font_scale=1.2)
    sns.heatmap(r2_matrix, annot=True, xticklabels=columns, yticklabels=columns, cmap='viridis')
    plt.title("R² Matrix Heatmap")
    plt.show()

# 3. value count plot
def plot_value_counts(df: pd.DataFrame, max_cols:int = 3):
    num_features = len(df.columns)
    ncols = min(max_cols, num_features)
    nrows = math.ceil(num_features / ncols)
    
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=(5*ncols, 4*nrows))
    axs = axs.flatten() if num_features > 1 else [axs]
    
    for i, col in enumerate(df.columns):
        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[col]):
            data = df[col].dropna()
            # Plot density histogram
            axs[i].hist(data, bins='auto', density=True, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
            # Plot vertical red dashed line for mean
            mean_val = data.mean()
            axs[i].axvline(mean_val, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, label=f"Mean: {mean_val:.2f}")
            # Overlay PDF using kernel density estimate
            sns.kdeplot(data, ax=axs[i], color='black', lw=2)
            axs[i].set_title(f"{col} (Histogram & PDF)")
            axs[i].set_xlabel("Value")
            axs[i].set_ylabel("Density")
            axs[i].legend()
        else:
            # For non-numeric columns, plot value counts
            counts = df[col].value_counts().sort_index()
            axs[i].bar(counts.index.astype(str), counts.values, color='skyblue')
            axs[i].set_title(f"{col} (Value Counts)")
            axs[i].set_xlabel("Value")
            axs[i].set_ylabel("Count")
            axs[i].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
    
    # Hide any unused subplots
    for j in range(i+1, len(axs)):
        axs[j].axis('off')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
# Assuming your DataFrame 'df' is already loaded:
r2_matrix = plot_cross(df)
plot_r2_heatmap(r2_matrix, df.columns)
plot_value_counts(df)

# Optionally, save the cleaned DataFrame to CSV
df.to_csv("cleaned_data.csv", index=False)

import yaml
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, Ridge, Lasso, ElasticNet
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor, GradientBoostingRegressor
from sklearn.svm import SVR
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, GridSearchCV
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# holds a registry of different regression models
class RegressionFactory:
    def __init__(self):
        '''Registry for modls'''
        self.models = {
            'linear': LinearRegression(),
            'ridge': Ridge(),
            'lasso': Lasso(),
            'elastic': ElasticNet(),
            'Random Forest': RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42),
            'Gradient Boosting': GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42),
            'Support Vector Regressor': SVR()
        }
        self.metrics = {}
    def register(self, name, model):
        self.models[name] = model
    def get(self, name):
        return self.models.get(name)
    def register_metrics(self, name, metrics):
        self.metrics[name] = metrics

# PipelineFactory that builds a pipeline with scaling and modeling.
class PipelineFactory:
    def __init__(self):
        '''Registry for pipelines'''
        self.pipelines = {}  
    def create_pipeline(self, model):
        '''Creates a pipeline with scaling and the given model.'''
        return Pipeline([
            ('scaler', StandardScaler()),
            ('model', model)
        ])
    def register(self, name, pipeline):
        self.pipelines[name] = pipeline
    def get(self, name):
        return self.pipelines.get(name)

def split_data(df: pd.DataFrame, target: str, features: list, **kwargs) -> dict:
    train, test = train_test_split(df, **kwargs)
    if features is None:
        features = df.drop(target, axis=1).columns.tolist()
    train_X = train[features]
    train_y = train[target]
    test_X = test[features]
    test_y = test[target]
    return {'train_X': train_X, 'train_y': train_y, 'test_X': test_X, 'test_y': test_y}

def train_pipelines(
    df: pd.DataFrame, 
    target: str, 
    features: list, 
    model_names: list,
    model_factory: RegressionFactory, 
    pipeline_factory: PipelineFactory,
    param_grids: dict = {}
    ) -> None:
    
    # get data
    dataset = split_data(df, target, features, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
    
    # train pipelines
    for model_name in model_names:
        # instantiate pipeline
        model = model_factory.get(model_name)
        pipeline = pipeline_factory.create_pipeline(model)
        grid_params = param_grids.get(model_name, {})
        # tune if tunable, else regular fit
        if grid_params:
            gs = GridSearchCV(pipeline, grid_params, cv=5)
            gs.fit(dataset['train_X'], dataset['train_y'])
            pipeline = gs.best_estimator_
            print(f"{model_name} pipeline tuned successfully, best parameters: {gs.best_params_}")
        else:
            pipeline.fit(dataset['train_X'], dataset['train_y'])
            print(f"{model_name} pipeline trained successfully (no tuning parameters)")
        # evaluate and register
        y_pred = pipeline.predict(dataset['test_X'])
        r2 = pipeline.score(dataset['test_X'], dataset['test_y'])
        mse = np.mean((y_pred - dataset['test_y'])**2)
        # Register pipeline and metrics
        pipeline_factory.register(model_name, pipeline)
        model_factory.register_metrics(model_name, {'r2': r2, 'mse': mse})

8. Determine if porosity shows a stronger dependency on any other property than indicated in problem 7. If so, develop an alternative regression model and report its R² and MSE values.¶

The results of training multiple tuned regression models for each possible predictor indicates that there is no stronger dependency on any other property for estimating porosity. This corroborates EDA results that showed Depth (ft) as the most correlated feature with Porosity.

Feature Importance results are found below.

# Instantiate factories and train pipelines with tuning functionality

target = 'Porosity (%)'
feature_set = [[feature] for feature in df.drop(target,axis=1).columns]

          'Gradient Boosting', 'Support Vector Regressor']
best_features = dict()
for features in feature_set:
    
    train_pipelines(df, target, features, models, model_factory,
                    pipeline_factory, param_grids)

    best_features[features[0]] = {

        'mse': model_factory.metrics[best_model]['mse'],
        'model': best_model
    }
    print(f"Best model for feature set {features}: {best_model} with R^2: {model_factory.metrics[best_model]['r2']}")
